newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IMF begins overview of loan facility to Hungary.
newsitem.headline: IMF begins overview of loan facility to Hungary.

text.p: A visiting delegation of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has begun the third overview of a 264.2 million SDR, 23-month stand-by loan facility to Hungary, the Finance Ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.
During their visit, the experts will meet government, central bank and social security officials, the statement said.
It added that the IMF experts will present their report to the IMF's board, probably in September.
Hungary concluded the loan agreement with the IMF in March 1996.
The country declared after signing the loan that it needed the agreement only because it was an important international seal of approval on Hungary's economic policies.
Following the previous overviews of the loan, Hungary could have drawn three tranches from the facility, but it did not use the opportunity, the statement said.
The daily Magyar Hirlap said the IMF experts on Monday met the leaders of Hungary's six largest trade union groups and inquired mainly about wages and inflation.

Hungary plans to cut average inflaton to about 18 percent this year and to some 13.5 percent in 1998 from 23.6 percent in 1996, while real wages are expected to rise by two percent both in 1997 and in 1998, after a five percent fall in 1996.
